answer: An agent network curbs Sybil attacks by tying identities to radio time-of-flight multilateration. Verifiers across a shipping wharf and an adjacent canyon track picosecond RF scatter off an industrial relic. Fabricating identities forces an attacker to deploy discrete physical transceivers across distinct coordinates, imposing real hardware and deployment costs. However, moving obstacles can distort reflection paths, causing temporary verification failures for legitimate nodes.
